title: Fronted Topics and Clitic Pronouns in Debate

sections.content:
In formal debate, speakers often place a known idea first to set the topic before answering it: *Ese argumento ya lo conozco*, *La réplica la preparó ayer*. Putting a known object at the start of the sentence is called left dislocation. Because the object appears before the verb as the topic, Spanish requires a matching clitic pronoun (*lo, la, los, las* for direct objects; *le, les* for indirect objects) directly before the verb.

You know fronting for emphasis from B2 Unit 1 (*Crucial fue la intervención*). Fronting an object works differently, and the rule separates two structures cleanly:
• Fronted **topic** (an object already known from the conversation): the clitic is required (*Ese informe lo firmó la directora*; *Ese informe firmó la directora* is wrong as a topic).
• Fronted **contrastive focus** (new or contrasted quantity/item): no clitic for the fronted item (*Un solo dato pido, no diez*).
• Fronted **indirect object**: the clitic *le / les* is required (*A los interlocutores les preocupa el enfoque*).

sections.title: Topic dislocation (clitic required) vs. contrastive focus (no clitic)
rows: Ese razonamiento ya lo escuchamos antes.
Las preguntas las organiza el moderador.
Eso no lo dije yo en mi intervención.
Al interlocutor le faltó tiempo para la réplica.
Un minuto pido, no media hora.

items.spanish: Ese enfoque lo defendió el invitado al comienzo del debate.
items.english: That approach was defended by the guest at the start of the debate.

items.spanish: La réplica la guardo para mi siguiente turno de palabra.
items.english: I am saving the rebuttal for my next turn to speak.

items.spanish: A los dos invitados les pidió el moderador que respetaran el tiempo.
items.english: The moderator asked both guests to respect the time.

items.spanish: Eso no lo afirmé en mi primera intervención.
items.english: I did not claim that in my first contribution.

sections.content: English fronts a topic with no extra pronoun (*That report, the director signed yesterday*). In Spanish, leaving out *lo / la / los / las* with a known topic object sounds incomplete or ungrammatical. Check the gender and number of the fronted noun so the clitic matches it: *la intervención → la*, *los datos → los*, *eso → lo*.
